plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with slender silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields for essential oils, and highly attractive to bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Provence in France, southern England, Bulgaria, and temperate gardens across North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, English lavender is native to the western Mediterranean; Romans used it in bathing water, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning to wash.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and showy, many-petaled flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a super-hydrophobic surface that causes water to bead and roll off.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer through late summer (June to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Shallow ponds and wetlands across India, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and the Volga Delta in Russia; also grown in water gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; seeds around 1,300 years old recovered from an ancient lake bed in China were successfully germinated.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy prairie perennial with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping rosy-purple petals around a spiky orange-brown central cone. It thrives in full sun, tolerates drought, and attracts pollinators and finches in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn (June to September)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern North American prairies and open woodlands; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone. Native Americans used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head of the protea family, with a central cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by showy colored bracts. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and periodic fires in fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late autumn to spring, with peak flowering from about May to September and flowers seen in the winter during early July
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change his shape, reflecting the family's great diversity.
